_about: The Peloponnesian War, year by year (2026-10-25, on request). AUTHORED: which polis, island or region stood with Athens and which with Sparta in each campaign year (a change in autumn or winter counts from the next year), each span with the passage that says so: Thucydides (Crawley), Xenophon’s Hellenica (Brownson), Diodorus, and the Athenian Tribute Lists (IG I³ 259–290). `conf` (medium | low) marks a judgement; no `conf` is the text’s plain statement. READ by build-war-extents.js, which draws each entry from its Pleiades point (a polis: the land within radiusKm, default 12; on a shared island, within that island) or its whole OSM coast ring (an island), and Lacedaemon from OpenHistoricalMap. `enclave`: a fort or town that keeps its own ground inside the other side’s land. Uncovered years are neutral or unknown and draw nothing.

notes.athens: Athens and its empire, year by year: the land of every polis that stood with Athens in that campaign year (within 12 km or so of its town, Pleiades’ point) and every allied island whole, from Folio’s table of members with the passages that place each one (Thucydides, Xenophon, the Athenian Tribute Lists). It shows whose towns these were, not a frontier.
notes.sparta: Sparta and its allies, year by year: Lacedaemon (OpenHistoricalMap’s polygon, CC0) and the land of every polis that stood with Sparta in that campaign year (round its Pleiades point) or every allied island whole, from Folio’s table of members with the passages that place each one. It shows whose towns these were, not a frontier.

research:
CONVENTIONS. (1) A span's year shows the alignment at the end of that year's campaigning season. A change in summer counts from that year; a change in autumn or winter (Thucydides' winter X/X-1) counts from the next year. Hence Amphipolis, Torone, Argilus and the Acte towns are Spartan from -423 (they fell in early winter 424/3), Melos Athenian from -415 (surrendered winter 416/5), Rhodes, Cnidus, Oropus, Phocaea and Cyme from -411, Byzantium Athenian again from -408 (winter 409/8), and every defection after Aegospotami (autumn 405) from -404. The brief gave Amphipolis 424 and Melos 416; each span carries a 'when' field so the year can be moved if you prefer the event year. (2) A revolt put down in the same season is not shown (Mytilene, Methymna and Clazomenae in 412, Cyzicus and Lampsacus in 411, Mende in 423, Argos' oligarchic interlude of winter 418/7); each is in the entry's 'why' or 'note'. (3) Uncovered years mean neutral OR unknown; 'conf' (absent = high, else medium/low) marks spans resting on inference. (4) Tributaries with no recorded change are Athenian to -405 (conf medium), relying on Xen. Hell. 2.2.6 that the Greek world fell away 'immediately after the battle, with the exception of Samos', and Spartan in -404. Mainland Asian tributaries with no specific evidence (Teos, Myrina, Gryneum, Pitane, Elaea, Pygela, Myus, Caunus, Myndus, Termera, Caryanda, Ceramus, Phaselis, Lamponeia, Gargara, Neandreia, Sigeum, Cius) are covered only -431..-413, since the King's treaties of 412/1 claimed the cities of Asia (Thuc. 8.18) and their later status is unrecorded. Athens' tribute was replaced by a 5% harbour tax in 413 and no quota list survives after 415/4. (5) Tribute membership is checked against the readable entries of IG I³ 279 (433/2), 280 (432/1) and the wartime lists 281–290 in the IG digital edition; each tributary cites the list in which I actually read its name.
DEPARTURES FROM THE BRIEF / JUDGMENT CALLS. Rhegium was an Athenian ally only 427-424; in 415 it declared neutrality (Thuc. 6.44) and is absent from the catalogue of 7.57. Sicily: Thuc. 3.86 says the Dorian Sicilian cities except Camarina were in the Lacedaemonian confederacy from the start of the war, so Syracuse, Gela, Selinus and (low confidence, Thucydides' generalisation) Acragas are Spartan-side -431..-425; the first Athenian intervention (Leontini, Naxos, Catana, Camarina, Rhegium) is -427..-425, ending at the Peace of Gela (summer 424); Locri fought on and made peace only in 422 (5.5). Elis is not covered after 418: the Eleans left the allied army before Mantinea but are absent from the Spartan levy of 413/2 (8.3), and Sparta was still at odds with Elis after the war. The Achaeans other than Pellene are not covered (2.9: 'afterwards followed by the rest', undated). Corinth is uncovered 421-419 (allied with Argos without joining Athens: 5.31, 5.48). The Ozolian Locrians are Spartan from 426 only; 3.95 calls them allies of Athens in 426, but their earlier status is not stated. Thera joined by the 25th tribute year (430/29: IG I³ 281), dated -429. Cythera: Athenian 424-413 is attested (Cytherians in Athens' ranks at Syracuse, 7.57; not returned in 421 as the treaty required); its return to Sparta is undated (Spartan by 393, Xen. Hell. 4.8.8), entered from -412 with low confidence. Plataea after 427 is drawn Spartan-side (land given to Thebes). Cos -407 Spartan is low confidence (Diodorus 13.69 has Alcibiades ravaging Cos; Lysander called there). Andros' revolt is undated before 407; Abdera's before 407 (dated -411 low). Hestiaea/Oreus is assumed lost after Aegospotami. Lemnos, Imbros and Scyros (Athenian cleruchies) and Naupactus (Messenians) are left uncovered in 404. Methymna stays Spartan from Callicratidas' capture (406) since Eteonicus fell back there after Arginusae.
GEOGRAPHY. Pleiades ids were matched against the full Pleiades export and every id was re-fetched from https://pleiades.stoa.org/places/<id>/json: all 268 reprPoints agree with 'lonlat' to 0.01°. Cnidus uses the earlier city at Burgaz (599576): Pleiades and current scholarship put the move to Tekir in the 4th century. Clazomenae uses the island city (550651): Thuc. 8.14 says the Clazomenians lived on the island in 412. Lacedaemon's id is Sparta (570685), for reference only; draw it from OpenHistoricalMap. Lesbos and Euboea have several poleis, so each carries 'island' and a radius; Rhodes, Chios, Samos, Corcyra, Cephallenia, Zacynthus, Ceos, Carpathos and Thasos are drawn whole because the island changed side as one (Ceos' four towns and Carpathos' towns are not split). Ozolian Tritaea (541166 'Triteia') and Ipnus (540828 'Hypnia?') are uncertain identifications in Pleiades/Barrington. Sane is the Acte town (501599); Thucydides' Sane of 4.109/5.18. The tribute lists' 'Sanaier' could be it or the Pallene Sane. Two Dikaias and two Neapoleis are both tributaries and both included.
NOT INCLUDED. Persia and the satrapies (allied to Sparta from 412), Macedonia (Perdiccas changed side repeatedly), the Aetolians, Chaonians, Sicels, Odomantians, Edonian Myrcinus, Crete, Melos before 416, and Panactum after it was razed (420). Athenian forts with no town (Delphinium on Chios 412-407, Sidussa and Pteleum in the Erythraeid, the Laconian fort opposite Cythera of 413, Lecythus) are left out.
